title: Monitoring, backup and rollback: health probes, scheduled backups, one-click rollback with an incident card
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04; owner chose Stage 1 + Stage 2 scope).

VISION Stage 2 'monitoring, backup, and rollback' and the Operations verifier row ('deployment, telemetry, backup, rollback, incident handling - blocks at Gate 3'). Re-measured 2026-09-04: `/health/read` reports the daemon's own health only; there is no probe of a deployed product, no backup schedule, no rollback kind.

FEATURE: (a) MONITORING: for every environment with a deploy receipt, the daemon probes the health URL on a durable schedule (default 60 s, per-environment setting), records `moe-health-probe/1` {environment, sha, status, latencyMs, at} in a bounded ring (last 1440) and derives UP / DEGRADED / DOWN; three consecutive failures raise ONE Needs-you INCIDENT card 'production unhealthy since <t>: roll back to <prev sha>?' with the last error line. (b) BACKUP: scheduled backups of the project store and, per environment with a database, `pg_dump` (`<project>/.moe-next/backups/...`, sha256, retention N); every backup receipt is proven restorable by a restore-to-temp check whose sha256 is recorded. (c) ROLLBACK: `deployment.rollback {environment, toReceiptRef}` (human-only) redeploys the previous image/sha (atomic replace, same health probe) and optionally restores the database backup taken at that deploy; receipt `moe-rollback-receipt/1`. (d) UI: the Deployments card shows UP / DEGRADED / DOWN with the last probe + a latency sparkline (last hour), the backups list with restore-proof state, Rollback arm/confirm; Needs-you incident card with Roll back / Dismiss; the Health screen gains an 'Environments' section. Refusals: ROLLBACK_RECEIPT_UNKNOWN, ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING, BACKUP_FAILED, PROBE_URL_MISSING.
definitionOfDone: Probe loop test with a fake target: UP -> DOWN after 3 failures raises exactly one incident card (no duplicate on continued failure) and recovery closes it; the ring is bounded at 1440; probes survive a daemon restart from durable records (no probe lost, no double schedule).
Backup test: store + pg_dump backups written on schedule; restore-to-temp sha256 equality recorded per receipt; retention prunes to N with the pruned refs listed in the receipt.

`deployment.rollback` published human-only, MCP-excluded, with the full roster backfill and bidirectional roster tests; the offline test asserts the previous image tag is redeployed and the DB restore is applied only when requested; ROLLBACK_RECEIPT_UNKNOWN, ROLLBACK_IMAGE_MISSING, BACKUP_FAILED, PROBE_URL_MISSING asserted with code + layer.
Deployments card + incident card + Health 'Environments' section against a REAL daemon (Playwright; count line quoted).

Live drive: a deployed PREVIEW environment probed for at least 10 minutes, a forced failure raises the incident card, rollback restores the previous sha - probe ring excerpt + receipts in a row comment.
Runbook + README; gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.

implementationPlan.description: ADVERSARIAL PASS OVER THE COMPOSED FEATURE, recorded in a step note. This is an INCIDENT feature: every defect here surfaces when someone is already having a bad day. (a) THE FLAPPING ENVIRONMENT: an environment that fails three probes, recovers, fails three again — does it raise a second incident, or reuse a closed one, and does the operator see a history or just the latest? Child 1 proved one-incident-per-outage; nobody proved the behaviour across repeated outages. (b) ROLLBACK TO A ROLLBACK: after rolling back from sha B to sha A, what does the 'previous' receipt point at, and can the operator roll forward again? A rollback that makes B unreachable strands them. (c) THE PROBE AND THE ROLLBACK DISAGREEING: the rollback redeploys and waits for health; the probe loop is also running. Can they race such that the probe records DOWN for the new deployment and raises an incident for a rollback that actually succeeded? (d) A BACKUP RESTORED INTO THE WRONG ENVIRONMENT: child 2 restores to temp for proof, but the rollback's optional DB restore targets a real database — confirm the environment is bound to the backup and cannot be crossed. That is the one path here that destroys data rather than availability. Where an answer is 'not covered', add it to the owning child's DoD or as a comment here (global rail 21).

(c) PROBE vs ROLLBACK RACE — cannot raise a false incident, closed twice: the unique index blocks a second open incident while the first is open, and the deploy path never leaves the environment with no container serving (deploy-rollback.test.ts:162).
